audits.summary:
I found no leak in Ridge's pm25 data path at leads 0, 6 or 12. Ridge's columns, offset, training rows, tuning window and test rows match the signed protocol, and I checked them against the exported files across all 127 groups. Nothing in its feature matrix comes from at or after the target step, or after the issue step at leads 6 and 12. The offset is built only from labels at or before each cut. Tuning ran on lead 0 only and finished before the test labels were opened. Ridge gets no column outside the pm25 ban list's keep and watch sets.

There are three preregistered differences between Ridge and our model. Their measured effect is small or very small:
- Ridge trains one model on all groups, including the test unit's own group. Our model's router never uses its own group's trees.
- Ridge uses ctx:lat and ctx:month directly as inputs. These carry about 0.1-0.4% of its weight.
- The log_c constant used in tuning comes from the fit cut: c = 1.5. Using only rows up to the guard cut it would be 1.55.

Evidence that the win is real: on the same 68,559 inner rows, before any test label was read, Ridge already beat our adopted arm, 3.3275 vs 3.3395 MAE. It picked from 16 candidates against our 282.

What drives Ridge: its largest coefficients are on hist_mean_60 and hist_mean_12 (positive) and hist_mean_all (negative). That is a correction of the 2003-2019 normal toward each unit's recent level. It uses only labels at or before the issue step, and our trees get the same columns.

Parity checks P1-P15 do not cover four things: the values of test-row and score-surface features, the context columns, the normals on the fit rows, and the pattern of missing values. My own checks closed the normals and the time alignment.

findings.claim: (1) Ridge's input columns are the same at leads 0, 6 and 12: 122 tree columns (116 kept features plus hist_last_1/2/3, hist_mean_12/60/all), the 2 context columns ctx:month and ctx:lat, and the link-space normal, which is both the last column and the fixed offset. Ridge adds one missing flag per column that has gaps in its fit rows. Every column is a keep or watch verdict in the pm25 ban.yaml; no ban or conditional column reaches Ridge, and every keep or watch column is exported.

Harness feature list is x__ then c__ (D:\treeroute\rivals_build\rivals\harness.py:720-722). The normal is appended as __normal__ (models.py:1067); target = link(y) - normal (models.py:346-349); prediction = normal + f(X) (models.py:1145-1146). Saved model_ridge.json: 170/179/206 design columns, 45/54/81 missing flags, nothing dropped. Export writes x__/c__/nfit__ for train and test rows (export.py:1155-1164, 1197-1205) and h__/ngd__ for the guard-side rows (export.py:1177-1183).

audits.summary:
I found no leak and no unfair advantage behind Ridge's PM2.5 result. Ridge's fit, tuning, refit and scoring all use the same rows, columns, normals, cuts, guard rule and metric code as our model. Test labels were first opened about an hour after the picks were locked and after every Ridge prediction file had been written and hashed.

I rescored the board myself from the saved files and got the same numbers exactly:
- lead 0: d = -0.161716 [-0.342313, +0.018881]
- lead 6: d = -0.246646 [-0.421859, -0.071434]
- lead 12: d = -0.427444 [-0.636622, -0.218265] against our headline answer, and -0.184325 [-0.326148, -0.042501] raw against raw

There is evidence the win is real and was visible before the test period. On the same 68,559 inner rows (2017-2019), Ridge's inner MAE of 3.327456 was already below our best inner candidate (log_c_corrector_unweighted, 3.339518).

Two things make the result look worse for us than the typical region:
- **Lead 12 decline.** Our own guard failed there (3.580670 vs 3.552497), so our headline falls back to the normal (4.084). That accounts for 0.243 of the 0.427 gap, but Ridge still wins raw against raw.
- **A few regions carry the win.** At lead 0, North China Plain alone gives -9.45 of the -20.54 summed group difference. The median group difference is -0.008, and without the 10 regions where Ridge gains most, ours is ahead by +0.044.

Ridge's biggest effects are the history columns (all-time mean -0.32, 60-month mean +0.20, 12-month mean +0.12), and its lead grows every test year (lead 0: -0.04 in 2020 to -0.31 in 2023). My reading, which I have not tested, is that Ridge carries forward the recent PM2.5 decline, mainly in China, that the pre-2020 normal misses. That would be a modelling difference, not a leak.

findings.claim: Ridge's scaling, missing-value fill, offset, back-transform and clipping are all fitted on the training rows only, and use the engine's own link functions.
findings.evidence: D:\treeroute\rivals_build\rivals\models.py:1035-1095: the column means, missing flags and kept columns are computed only from the fit rows. models.py:1098-1146: the cross-products, the column scales and the intercept come from the fit rows, and the score rows reuse those numbers. models.py:328-350: the training label is log(y+c) minus the normal. models.py:353-362: a prediction is the normal plus the fitted part, turned back with exp(z)-c (engine layer/links.py). models.py:1264-1273: predictions are clipped to [0, inf). The run's c is 1.5 at every lead (derived.json R23 lead 0, 6 and 12). Cross-check in lead_<L>\model_ridge.json: the intercept is 0.000000000, equal to the mean of log(y+1.5) minus the normal over the refit rows I recomputed. The normal column's mean 2.683739763 and sd 0.743836 (lead 0) equal those of the refit rows in rivals_scratch lead_0_refit.index.parquet; leads 6 and 12 match the same way. No test prediction went below zero before the clip; the smallest is 0.605 (lead 0).

findings.claim: Tuning used only data from before 2020: the training rows end at the nowcast guard cut and the score rows are the inner window. The alpha grid is fixed and the pick is the lowest inner MAE.
findings.evidence: models.py:45 sets the alpha grid {0.1, 1, 10, 100, 1e3, 1e4, 1e5, 1e6}. harness.py:1745-1800 and 1623-1705 fit each trial on the 'tune' set and score it only on 'inner'. harness.py:1192-1205 picks the lowest MAE, breaking ties by link order, then grid order, then the smaller alpha. lead_0_tune.index.parquet holds 2,133,214 rows with time 24037-24204, ending at the guard cut 24204. The inner set has 68,559 rows (n_inner in trials.csv). The log_c alpha curve is flat, from 3.3370 at alpha 0.1 to 3.3275 at alpha 1000, so the pick gains almost nothing from selection luck. The one cross-cut input is c: tuning reads the fit-cut c (harness.py:1164-1166). It equals 1.5 at every cut, the engine does the same, and the protocol (section 3, item 8) discloses it.

That pattern reads the recent level against the long-run level. All of these columns are known at issue time (see the history check above). That this explains the win is my interpretation, not something I tested.

audits.summary: I found no leak and no unfair advantage. Ridge's win is real, and why it wins is clear from the numbers (post-hoc diagnosis, labelled as such). (a) Ridge saw the same data we did: the same 91,440 test rows in the same order, the same labels, and a normal that is exactly ours (max gap 0). Its 116 driver columns plus 6 history columns are all on our keep/watch list, and none is banned or conditional. There are no AOD, CAMS, MERRA-2 or other aerosol columns. Drivers at lead L are read at the issue step t-L (100% match). hist_last_1 equals y(t-L) exactly (y(t-1) at lead 0). Every training row is dated at or before its cut. Tuning used the earlier guard-cut normal (100% of rows). The picks were locked at 05:21:41Z, before any test label was opened (06:27:13Z), and the ledger shows only that one lock. Re-scoring both models from the saved row-level predictions gives exactly the board's numbers. (b) How Ridge wins: its largest coefficients form a linear trend detector. hist_mean_all is negative, hist_mean_60 and hist_mean_12 are positive (standardised -0.319/+0.198/+0.116 at lead 0), so it lowers its forecast for places where the recent level sits below the long-run level. It also gets a roughly uniform -4% shift from slow climate indices (PDO, global tropical SST anomaly). Both are linear extrapolations that trees cannot make, while our model stays anchored to a normal frozen at 2019. (c) The win is concentrated. At lead 0 Ridge wins only 65 of 127 groups (median group difference -0.008). north_china_plain alone moves the mean difference by -0.074 of the -0.162: there our model predicts about 58 ug/m3 against observed 40-46, and has a +16 bias even with last month's value in hand. With the 3 Chinese groups left out, lead 0 is d -0.042 [-0.128, +0.043]. At leads 6 and 12 the win is broad: Ridge wins 85 of 127 groups, and it still wins after dropping China (d -0.130 and -0.093, both intervals below 0). (d) The edge grows with test year and with how steeply a group was declining before 2020. It was already visible before test labels at leads 6 and 12 (the pre-test check window: Ridge 0.11-0.12 ahead). At lead 0 the pre-test window was nearly a tie (Ridge 0.012 ahead).

The strongest remaining case is not a leak, and it is small. It comes from five points, all shared by Ridge and our model:
(1) Some raw driver stores are processed using their whole record, and I did not audit that processing. This covers how SPI was calibrated, how AMO was detrended, how deeprec_twsa was trained, and that WorldPop 2021-23 is extrapolated. These columns carry only 2.8-4.1% of Ridge's standardized weight. They are lagged correctly, both models get them, and I did not audit the processing inside those stores.
(2) On training rows the offset (the normal) is in-sample. It includes the row's own label and labels after that row's issue step, up to the fit cut. Read literally, the owner's definition ("post-issue information in the offset of a training row") covers this. But the engine does the same for our model (R15). It carries no 2020-23 information, and on test rows the normal uses only labels at or before the cut.
(3) Ridge pools all 12,700 units, including other units of the test group. I measured this with an exact leave-one-group-out refit. It changes no verdict.
(4) The slow climate indices act as a level or trend term: about -0.02 to -0.06 log units on test rows and -0.01 to -0.03 on 2017-19 training rows. They are legitimate, lagged, on the keep list, and both models get them.
(5) At lead 0 the nowcast uses weather from month t by design, for both models.
A weaker point: the lead-0 test feature files carry hist_last_1 = y(t-1), so 47 of the 48 test months' labels can be read without opening the label column. challenges.why_it_fails_or_holds:
The objection does not hold. Every extra advantage Ridge had, when removed, moves the result by 0.026 MAE or less, and no verdict changes.

**How I tested it.** I reproduced Ridge exactly: the same design rules, alpha 1000 and the log_c link with c = 1.5. I rebuilt it from sufficient statistics collected in one memmap pass over each lead's refit .f32, per group. The full refit matches the saved model_ridge.json coefficients to within 1.3e-9 relative, and the saved pre-clip test predictions to within 1.3e-11, at all three leads. I then refit these variants:
- **LOGO:** the test unit's whole group removed.
- **LOGO+own:** the group removed, then the scored unit's own pre-cut rows added back. This is exactly what our router sees.
- **Strict:** LOGO+own, plus no ctx:lat and no missing flags.

**Results (pooled MAE, then d = rival minus our pinned model, mean over groups with group-jackknife 95% interval):**

| 0 | 3.4264, d -0.162 [-0.342, +0.019] | 3.4524, d -0.136 [-0.319, +0.048] | 3.4511 | 3.4488, d -0.139 [-0.322, +0.044] | 3.5881 |

| 12 | 3.6561, d -0.184 [-0.326, -0.043] | 3.6677 | 3.6672 | 3.6654, d -0.175 [-0.314, -0.037] | 3.8405 pinned |

At lead 12, the strict variant against our headline answer (4.0836) gives d -0.418 [-0.625, -0.212]. Dropping only lat, or only the flags and context, changes MAE by 0.002 or less, and Ridge actually gets slightly better without them.

**Other checks I did myself on the files:**
- **Same rows:** the outer join on (unit, time, lead) is 91,440/91,440 at every lead, 91,428 rows have labels, and all 127 groups have equal weight. My own MAE and jackknife reproduce the board exactly.
- **Same columns:** the 124 rival columns are 116 keep/watch columns from ban.yaml, the 2 context columns, and the 6 history columns, which are exactly the run's plan.json history_columns. No ban or conditional column reaches Ridge, and no keep/watch column is missing.
- **Inputs that drive the win:** hist_last_1/2/3 and hist_mean_12/60/all on all 91,440 lead-0 test rows equal my recomputation from labels dated strictly before t, with max relative error 6e-8 on the means and 0 on the lags.
- **Preregistered choices:** the alpha grid, the mean fill with flags, and the context columns are all in the signed protocol (section 2 C1; section 3 items 2, 6 and 8).
- **Guard:** Ridge faced the same guard as ours, and it passed at every lead. At lead 12 our decline costs us 0.243, but raw against raw Ridge still wins.

**Reading.** The lead 6 and 12 losses are real and fair. Lead 0 stays CANNOT TELL, so Ridge has not won there.
remaining_gaps: Test-row feature values were not compared byte-for-byte with what our own test pass used, because the run saved no test features. This is only closed indirectly. The export calls the engine's own RunState.build_pool and history_block. The three engine hops carry pm25 smoke proofs that the prediction files are byte-identical. In my fresh_hist.py check, our lead-0 correction (ours minus trees-off, in log space) correlates with last month's anomaly at r = 0.42/0.37/0.27/0.33 in 2020-2023, which fits fresh test-period history. Weather persistence could also explain part of that correlation.

The LOGO variants keep the pinned alpha of 1000 and are not re-tuned on the inner window. The inner-MAE curve is flat (3.337 at alpha 0.1, 3.327 at 1000), so this is unlikely to matter. That is my judgement; I did not test it.
I did not refit an identity-link Ridge on test rows. I did not audit RF or LightGBM, and I did not re-read the guard and verdict code. I used the board's verdict wording.

I did not audit whether the lead-0 non-history columns (for example annual covariates or centred indices) carry information from after t. A leak there would reach both models equally, and a Ridge with the history columns removed loses its edge (see the explanation), so such columns are not what drives the win.
The training-row normal includes each row's own label (in-sample R15 normal). Both models share this. It is a disclosure item, not a fairness gap.
